title: What If the Nile Dried Up Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if the Nile dried up tomorrow? Nearly everyone in Egypt depends on it.
Egypt gets about 18 millimeters of rain a year. The Nile supplies roughly nine-tenths of its water.
Almost everyone lives in the Nile Valley and Delta, on only about 4 percent of Egypt's land.
Within days, irrigation would stop. Agriculture uses about 86 percent of the country's water.
Of Egypt's 3.4 million hectares of irrigated farmland, about 85 percent sits in the valley and delta.
The desert already covers the other 96 percent. Without the river, the green strip would shrink fast.
